newsitem.title: USA: Lawyers prepare to break down Simpson testimony.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers prepare to break down Simpson testimony.

text.p: Lawyers for the plaintiffs in O.J. Simpson's wrongful-death case were spending the weekend working out their strategy to tear down the good-guy image projected by the ex-football star during his testimony on Friday.
Simpson, who returned to the witness stand for the second time in the civil suit against him, repeatedly denied ever hitting his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson.
He painted her as a troubled woman with wild mood swings and said she pursued him after their divorce. He said she also had confided in him about becoming pregnant by another man.

Legal experts were mixed in their opinions as to the effect of Simpson's testimony on the mostly white jury. Some said he ran the risk of alienating the panel by criticising his ex-wife, others said he came across as a sincere, caring person.

Simpson, who was acquitted in October 1995 in the June 12 1994, murders of his ex-wife and her friend, Ron Goldman, was one of the last defence witnesses scheduled to testify in the civil suit brought by the victims' families. He was due to resume his testimony on Monday.

Daniel Petrocelli, the lead lawyer for the plaintiffs, had called Simpson to the witness stand in November for two-and-a-half days of grueling examination. He was spending the weekend discussing strategy with his team of attorneys in a hotel across the street from the Santa Monica courthouse, where the trial is taking place.

Petrocelli won praise from legal analysts for his questioning of Simpson the first time around, eliciting from him a series of denials that he ever hit his ex-wife and an admission that he could not remember when he suffered a crucial cut on his left hand on the night of the murders.

Petrocelli indicated on Friday he might have another go at Simpson, telling Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki that he could possibly bring the defendant back in the rebuttal phase of the trial next week to confront him with 30 photographs of him at a Buffalo Bills National Football League game in 1993 wearing Italian designer Bruno Magli shoes with distinctive soles.
Experts have testified that those soles were the ones that left a trail of bloody shoeprints leading from the murder scene outside Nicole Brown Simpson's apartment.
A defence photographic analyst testified that another photograph taken at the same game by a different photographer was a fake.

But Friday was Simpson's day to shine before the jury. Looking calm and composed, his voice resounding through the crowded courtroom, Simpson expressed frustration about his ex-wife's sometimes erratic behaviour.
At one point only a few months before the June 1994 murders, Simpson said he called her mother and said, "Something is going on and I'm concerned about it."

In testimony that could further sully his ex-wife's image to the jury, Simpson told of how she had called him in 1992 after their breakup and confided that she had become pregnant by another man. In opening arguments last October, Baker told jurors Nicole Brown Simpson aborted the pregnancy.
Also in 1992, Simpson said that one day when he went to Nicole Brown Simpson's apartment, he glanced through the window and saw her performing oral sex on her boyfriend.
"Did you get in a rage?" Baker asked.
Simpson testified that it was his ex-wife who pursued him after their divorce, seeking a reconciliation and not the other way around, as the plaintiffs had contended.
